overall.sentence: The closest earlier paper, the cited Xia et al. 2025 (arXiv:2508.02662, ref. [28]), already tuned twisted WSe2 through the twist angle and mapped its superconducting phase diagram by transport; what this paper adds is tracking the displacement-field-induced, AFM-adjacent superconducting pocket continuously from 5° to 3.8° across several devices, with twist-angle-resolved FRG and Hartree-Fock theory.

assessment.claim: Introduction: the impact of the twist angle on superconductivity in tWSe2 remains unknown
assessment.note: The cited ref. [28] (posted August 2025) tunes moiré WSe2 bilayers through the twist angle and maps the superconducting phase diagram around ν = 1 by transport; the impact is studied, though in a different region of the phase diagram.

assessment.claim: Headline (claims 1 and 2): the superconducting pocket and AFM region evolve smoothly from 5° to 3.8°, connecting the 3.65° and 5° phase diagrams
assessment.note: Same system and method as ref. [28], which also varies twist angle; new here is following the high-displacement-field, AFM-adjacent pocket of the 5° device continuously to small angles and showing that it connects to the 3.65° phenomenology (judged from abstracts).

assessment.claim: 3. Below about 4.3° a half-filling insulator appears only in a narrow displacement-field window, indicating moderate rather than Mott-like interactions
assessment.note: Ref. [28] and ref. [1] (2405.14784) already report a ν = 1 insulator in tWSe2 interpreted near a bandwidth-tuned Mott transition in the moderate-correlation regime; new here is its twist-angle onset and narrow-D window across devices, with an interpretation that leans away from Mott physics.

assessment.claim: 4. Superconductivity always borders the AFM phase, suggesting spin-fluctuation pairing
assessment.note: The authors' own 5° paper (ref. [2]) and cited theory (2409.16114, ref. [34]) already tie the superconductor to AFM order and intervalley antiferromagnetic fluctuations; new here is that the adjacency holds at every angle from 5° to 3.8°.

assessment.claim: 5. FRG and Hartree-Fock on a three-orbital model reproduce the twist-angle evolution
assessment.note: The model and FRG method are the authors' own (ref. [32]); the arXiv query targeting twist-angle-resolved FRG/HF theory failed (HTTP 429), so the search on this claim is too weak to support no_precedent_found.

positioning: The paper sits between the two original tWSe2 superconductivity reports (3.65°, ref. [1]; 5°, ref. [2]) and the cited Xia et al. 2025 (ref. [28]), which already used the twist angle to tune tWSe2 into a moderate-correlation regime near a Mott insulator at ν = 1 and reported Tc up to about 6% of the effective Fermi temperature. What the searches show this paper adds is a multi-device map following the AFM-adjacent superconducting pocket from 5° down to 3.8°, with matched FRG and Hartree-Fock calculations; the framing that the twist-angle dependence is unknown, and the contrast between its Tc/TF below 1% and ref. [28]'s cuprate-like picture, are not addressed. Sources: arXiv API (5 successful queries; 3 failed with rate limits) and the paper's reference list.

issues.claim: The impact of the twist angle on superconductivity in tWSe2 has not been studied.
issues.headline: Cited Xia et al. 2025 already tuned superconductivity with twist angle
issues.issue: The introduction says the impact of the twist angle on superconductivity in tWSe2 remains unknown, and the abstract frames the field as two angles, 3.65° and 5°. The paper's own ref. [28] (Xia et al., arXiv:2508.02662, posted August 2025) tuned tWSe2 through the twist angle and mapped the superconducting phase diagram, and Fig. 2b already plots one of its devices. A referee from that community will read the sentence as overlooking that work.

evidence.quote: The impact of the twist angle on superconductivity in tWSe2 remains unknown and it is not clear if the two experimentally observed superconductors share the same origin
evidence.location: Introduction, last paragraph of the left column

issues.fix: Acknowledge that ref. [28] varied the twist angle near ν = 1 and state the open question more narrowly: how the high-displacement-field, AFM-adjacent superconductor of the 5° device evolves and whether it connects to the small-angle phenomenology.

edit.before: The impact of the twist angle on superconductivity in tWSe2 remains unknown and it is not clear if the two experimentally observed superconductors share the same origin
edit.after: Although twist angle has been used to tune tWSe2 toward a Mott insulator near half filling [28], how the displacement-field-induced superconductor adjacent to AFM order evolves with twist angle remains unknown, and it is not clear if the two experimentally observed superconductors share the same origin

issues.claim: Based on band-theory superfluid stiffness and Tc/TF, the superconductivity is in the weak-coupling BCS limit at all twist angles.
issues.headline: Weak-coupling conclusion not set against ref. [28]'s cuprate-like picture
issues.issue: Ref. [28] (Xia et al., arXiv:2508.02662) describes tWSe2 in this angle range as a moderately correlated, cuprate-like system with Tc reaching about 6% of the effective Fermi temperature. This paper finds Tc/TF below 1% and concludes weak-to-moderate, BCS-like pairing, but does not say why the two estimates differ by several times, which a referee will ask.

evidence.quote: reflecting values that suggest the superconductor remains in the weak to moderate correlation regime
evidence.location: Superconductivity versus twist angle, discussion of Fig. 2d

issues.fix: Add a sentence comparing the Tc/TF estimate with that of ref. [28], stating how the Fermi temperatures were defined in each (band-structure TF here versus an effective TF there) and whether the two are consistent.
